key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence can non-destructively separate interface- and bulk-dominated degradation in perovskite solar cells, revealing that PEABF4 initially passivates the ETL/perovskite interface but thermal aging spreads recombination deeper into the absorber.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical depth-sensitive diagnostic for optimizing interfacial passivation and tracking stability losses in perovskite device stacks under thermal stress.
method: Used wavelength-dependent PL excitation to probe different absorption depths in the perovskite stack.
Compared PEABF4-treated and untreated devices during thermal aging to localize recombination changes.
Supported interpretation with diffusion-recombination simulations linking PL decay to surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PL signatures showed reduced interfacial recombination after PEABF4 treatment, but faster degradation under thermal aging with recombination losses expanding from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber, consistent with simulation.
watch_item: PL-based depth attribution depends on model assumptions and optical penetration behavior, so quantitative conclusions should be validated against complementary structural or electrical measurements.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
